column26: Description

Create the GitHub repository, default branch, initial README, {{.gitignore}}, and the agreed folder structure.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Repository contains the target folders from Section 2 or a documented equivalent. - {{.gitignore}} excludes {{.env}}, virtual environments, caches, generated audio, model weights, and build artifacts. - README states project scope and English↔Hindi-only limitation. - All four members can clone the repository.

column1: Create Jira backlog and four sprints
column26:
Create all 40 items from this section, grouped into four sprints of 10. Assign every item to its sprint owner and add labels.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Exactly four sprints exist and each contains 10 top-level items. - All items have a description and acceptance criteria. - Dependencies and labels are recorded. - Team confirms the sprint order before implementation.

Write the concise functional/non-functional requirements and the user journeys for both directions.
*Acceptance criteria:* - English→Hindi and Hindi→English flows are separately documented. - Typed-text fallback is included. - Out-of-scope features are explicitly listed. - Team and instructor-facing demo criteria are documented.

Create {{docs/architecture.md}} describing browser, API, service layer, and STT/translation/TTS providers.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Architecture diagram matches Section 1. - Each model component has a replaceable provider boundary. - Request/response flow and error handling are documented. - No model-specific code is required by route handlers.

column1: Set up Python environment and dependencies
column26:
Add a minimal Python 3.11 backend environment and pin compatible core dependencies.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Setup instructions create and activate a virtual environment on Windows. - FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, pytest, and HTTP client dependencies are listed. - Heavy ML dependencies are separated or documented so a clean install can run tests without downloading models. - No machine-specific absolute paths are committed.

Add typed settings for host, port, log level, model IDs/paths, device selection, and upload limits.
*Acceptance criteria:* - {{.env.example}} contains safe example values only. - {{.env}} is ignored by Git. - Application has sensible local defaults. - Invalid configuration produces a readable startup error.

Create {{backend/app/main.py}}, app initialization, startup/shutdown hooks, and API router registration.
*Acceptance criteria:* - App starts with the documented Uvicorn command. - {{/docs}} is available. - Startup does not download models unexpectedly. - Importing the app does not require a GPU.

column1: Implement health endpoint and basic API tests
column26:
Add {{GET /api/health}} and tests for app startup and health response.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Endpoint returns JSON indicating service status. - Automated test passes without model downloads. - Failure output is understandable. - Test command is documented.

Create responsive page structure with project title, direction selector, mic/start/stop controls, typed-text fallback, transcript panels, and audio player placeholder.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Layout works on desktop browser. - Both language directions are selectable. - Controls have labels and disabled/loading states. - No model/API calls are required for this scaffold.

column1: Establish Git branching, PR and review rules
column26:
Document shared Git workflow and ensure every member can create a branch and open a PR.
*Acceptance criteria:* - {{main}} is protected if repository permissions allow. - PR template/checklist exists or the README contains the equivalent. - Each member makes one small test PR or contributes a reviewed change. - Team agrees never to force-push shared {{main}}.

Add Pydantic schemas for direction, source text, detected/source language, translated text, processing status, and error payloads.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Only {{en-to-hi}} and {{hi-to-en}} are accepted. - Empty/whitespace text is rejected with a useful 4xx response. - Response fields are documented. - Schema tests cover valid and invalid input.

column1: Define STT, translation and TTS provider interfaces
column26:
Define clear provider interfaces in {{backend/app/providers/}} with methods and typed return values.
*Acceptance criteria:* - STT accepts audio input and returns transcript plus language/metadata where available. - Translation accepts text and direction and returns translated text. - TTS accepts text and target language and returns audio bytes or a managed audio artifact. - Tests can inject fake providers without loading ML packages.

Implement deterministic fake STT, translation, and TTS providers for API tests and early UI integration.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Fake providers are clearly marked development/test-only. - Tests do not claim fake output is a real translation. - App can be run in mock mode from configuration. - No network or model download is required in mock mode.

column1: Verify and document Windows-compatible STT model
column26:
Evaluate {{faster-whisper}} model options for English/Hindi on Windows and the target GPU/CPU setup.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Official setup and license are checked. - A small model is selected for the first local smoke test. - CPU/GPU mode and VRAM/RAM observations are recorded. - Model loading is optional and isolated behind the STT provider.

Implement audio-to-transcript conversion with clear language handling and errors.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Adapter conforms to the STT interface. - Supports English and Hindi input. - Handles invalid/empty audio. - Unit tests use a mock; an optional local smoke test verifies real inference.

column1: Verify and document English↔Hindi translation model
column26:
Verify an IndicTrans2 implementation that supports both directions and can be installed in the team's Windows environment.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Model source, license, install steps, and language codes are documented. - One short English→Hindi and one Hindi→English example are manually checked. - Model loading/memory needs are recorded. - If the preferred implementation is incompatible, the team records a compatible replacement rather than blocking other work.

Implement the real translation adapter behind the provider interface.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Both directions are supported. - Direction-to-source/target language mapping is centralized. - Empty output and model exceptions are handled. - Unit tests cover both directions using fixtures/mocks; real-model checks are separate.

Orchestrate request validation, source/target mapping, translation provider call, response construction, and timing metadata.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Service has no dependency on FastAPI request objects. - Provider errors become controlled service errors. - Unit tests cover success and failure paths. - Logs do not print full user text by default.

Expose typed-text translation as a JSON API.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Endpoint returns source text, direction, target text, and status. - Invalid direction/text returns useful 4xx errors. - Provider failure returns a safe 5xx response without stack traces to the client. - OpenAPI docs show the request and response shape.

column1: Connect typed-text UI to translation API
column26:
Wire the text box and direction selector to {{/api/translate}}; display source and translated text.
*Acceptance criteria:* - User can translate typed text in both directions. - Loading and error states are visible. - Rapid repeat clicks do not corrupt the displayed result. - Manual test steps are added to {{docs/demo-checklist.md}}.

Evaluate a local TTS engine/model for both English and Hindi. Do not assume a model requiring Apple's MLX runtime works on Windows.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Model supports the needed languages and has a reviewed license. - Installation works on Windows or an explicitly documented supported runtime. - At least one English and one Hindi sample are generated. - Memory, startup time, synthesis latency, and voice quality observations are documented.

Implement text-to-speech behind the TTS provider interface.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Accepts target text and language. - Returns valid audio data with a known format/content type. - Handles unsupported language, empty text, and synthesis failures. - Unit tests use a fake provider; actual model test is optional/local.

column1: Add safe audio input validation and utilities
column26:
Validate uploaded audio type, size, duration where feasible, and safely manage temporary files/conversion.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Configured maximum upload size is enforced. - Unsupported/empty audio returns a clear client error. - Temporary files are cleaned up on success and failure. - Client-supplied filenames are never used as filesystem paths.

Accept audio upload and return transcript, language/direction metadata, and status.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Supports English and Hindi input. - Handles invalid media and STT failures cleanly. - Response shape is documented. - Tests cover mocked success and failure.

Accept source audio and direction, call STT then translation then TTS, and return text metadata plus generated audio in a documented response strategy.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Both directions are supported. - Source transcript and translated text are available to the client. - Audio is returned as a file response or via a documented job/result flow; do not invent a mixed JSON/binary format. - Errors identify the failed stage without exposing internal traces.

column1: Implement browser microphone permission and capture
column26:
Capture microphone audio only after explicit user action and handle browser permission denial.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Start/stop controls work in a supported browser. - Permission denial displays instructions and does not crash the UI. - Recording indicator is visible while recording. - Audio is stopped and media tracks are released when recording ends or page state resets.

column1: Upload captured audio and show source transcript
column26:
Send captured audio to the backend with the chosen direction and display the source transcript.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Correct direction is sent with every request. - User sees progress while processing. - Source transcript is displayed separately from translated text. - Network/API errors are recoverable.

Handle the generated audio response and provide play/pause/replay controls.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Successful response can be played in the browser. - Previous audio URLs/resources are cleaned up when replaced. - Audio format and content type match the API contract. - Failed playback shows a useful message.

column1: Add cancellation, reset and duplicate-request protection
column26:
Prevent accidental duplicate submissions and let the user reset the current result.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Submit is disabled or guarded while a request is active. - Reset clears visible transcripts/errors and stops audio playback. - Late responses do not overwrite a newer request. - Cancellation is implemented only where supported and documented.

Add integration tests using fake providers and manual smoke tests with real local models.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Tests verify audio input → transcript → translated text → audio response using fakes. - Both directions are tested. - Manual checklist covers microphone denial, invalid audio, slow model, and successful playback. - Actual-model smoke test instructions are separate from the default test suite.

column1: Improve end-to-end UI states and accessibility
column26:
Polish responsive layout, labels, keyboard navigation, loading indicators, transcript separation, and errors.
*Acceptance criteria:* - All controls have visible labels. - Focus indicators and keyboard operation are usable. - Loading/success/error states are distinguishable. - Desktop demo layout is clean and readable.

column1: Add request timeout and model failure handling
column26:
Add controlled timeout behavior and stable error mapping for STT, translation, and TTS failures.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Client receives a stable error schema. - No Python stack trace or sensitive local path is returned. - Timeout and provider errors are logged with request correlation IDs. - Tests cover each stage's failure.

column1: Add structured logging and timing metrics
column26:
Record request IDs, stage timings, outcome, and provider errors without recording raw audio or full transcript by default.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Logs distinguish STT, translation, and TTS timing. - Sensitive payloads are not logged by default. - Logs are useful for diagnosing failures. - Documentation explains where local logs are written.

column1: Add translation and transcription evaluation set
column26:
Create a small, consent-safe set of short English/Hindi test phrases and expected translations/transcripts for regression checks.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Includes both directions, short/long sentences, punctuation, numbers, and common names. - Dataset contains no private recordings or personal data. - Expected outputs are reviewed by a competent Hindi/English speaker. - Evaluation is documented as a small demo set, not a scientific benchmark.

column1: Add performance and memory benchmark script
column26:
Measure warm and cold model startup, per-stage latency, and peak memory for representative short utterances.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Script records environment, selected model IDs, device, and timing. - At least five short examples are measured for each direction when hardware allows. - Report identifies CPU/GPU configuration and limitations. - No hard performance guarantee is claimed without measurements.

Review upload limits, file type validation, temporary file cleanup, CORS, and error messages.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Only intended local frontend origins are allowed in development CORS configuration. - Upload size and type checks are tested. - Temporary files are cleaned even when inference fails. - No endpoint exposes arbitrary filesystem access.

column1: Write Windows setup and troubleshooting guide
column26:
Document a clean Windows setup, model downloads, environment variables, run commands, and common errors.
*Acceptance criteria:* - A teammate can follow the README on a clean clone. - Includes venv activation, dependency installation, backend start, frontend start, and tests. - Explains model download/cache and GPU fallback. - Documents the MLX incompatibility lesson and states that Apple-only runtime models must not be selected.

Document endpoints, request/response examples, architecture, limitations, and data handling.
*Acceptance criteria:* - API docs match actual implementation. - Setup and run instructions match current commands. - English↔Hindi scope and out-of-scope features are clear. - Known limitations and troubleshooting are included.

column1: Run full regression and acceptance checklist
column26:
Run automated tests and execute the final demo checklist on the target Windows machine.
*Acceptance criteria:* - All default automated tests pass. - Both directions work through typed-text and speech workflows. - Microphone denial, invalid input, and model failure are tested. - Any remaining known bug is documented and linked to Jira.

column1: Prepare final demo, release tag and handoff
column26:
Prepare a repeatable demo script, final architecture diagram, team contribution summary, and release tag.
*Acceptance criteria:* - Demo shows both English→Hindi and Hindi→English. - Repository has no secrets, model weights, private recordings, or generated test artifacts committed. - {{main}} is green and all accepted work is merged. - Release tag {{v1.0.0}} is created and final setup/demo steps are documented.

*Sprint 4 release checkpoint ---* {{v1.0.0}}*:* Freeze scope, run final regression, demo the product, and hand off the repository and documentation.
